explanations: luna: The prayer اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ directly voices the need for guidance onto a way. | terra: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ is the worshipper's direct request that God set the direction toward the straight road imagined in the section.

luna: The next verse defines the requested way through those favored and contrasts them with the angered and astray, giving moral content to the route in 1:6. | terra: The requested path is distinguished from the courses of غضب and ضلال, so guidance is completed by identifying divergent ends to avoid.
terra: God extends mockers in their transgression while they wander blindly, another exact case of a bad-directed course being allowed to continue.
terra: God sends guidance and promises freedom from fear and grief to whoever follows it, making the shown direction the opening of one outcome branch.
terra: Those who disbelieve and reject the signs become companions of the Fire, completing the opposed branch after guidance has arrived.

terra: At the struck rock كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ: groups know distinct drinking places before they depart, a structured division at water rather than the section's dispersal after one watering point.

luna: The question about the changed qibla and the statement that God guides whom He wills to a straight way connect physical orientation with the section's hidaya-as-direction gloss. | terra: The question about what turned people from their qibla is answered with God's ownership of east and west and His guidance to a straight road, joining face-direction, turning, and guidance.

luna: The verse says the former qibla was a test of who follows the Messenger; it makes turning toward a direction a choice that reveals one's course. | terra: The former qibla tests who follows the Messenger and who turns on his heels, and the change is difficult except for those God guides; it stages direction as a revealing fork.

luna: The command to face the Sacred Mosque wherever one is supplies the physical qibla orientation named alongside direction in the section's hidaya dictionary note. | terra: The repeated command to turn the face toward the Sacred Mosque makes direction, face, and qibla an enacted bodily orientation rather than an abstraction.
terra: The People of the Book do not share one another's qibla and will not follow the Messenger's, extending the qibla scene into explicitly persistent differences of direction.

luna: وجهة, turning toward it, and فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ occur together here, matching the section's meeting of direction and race. | terra: وَلِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ names each runner's direction, مُوَلِّيهَا names the turning, and فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ converts direction into a commanded race.

luna: Righteousness is not merely turning faces east or west; the verse defines it through belief, giving wealth, keeping promises, and patience. It links the section's qibla/direction gloss to its moral course of giving. | terra: Righteousness is not the mere turning of faces east or west but faith, giving cherished wealth, worship, fidelity, and patience; it prevents the section's directional image from becoming only spatial.
luna: Allah's stated wish for ease rather than hardship in fasting uses the same ease/difficulty contrast, though there it concerns a legal burden, not two moral paths.
terra: The command to spend is paired with the warning not to throw oneself into destruction, placing giving and a self-caused fall on opposite sides of one ayah.
luna: This person gives up himself seeking God's approval, a close parallel in aim to the section's giver who spends only seeking the Lord's face.
luna: قَد تَّبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ marks a boundary between right direction and error, illuminating the section's two distinct courses.
luna: Those who spend and do not follow the gift with reminders or injury receive reward from their Lord; this directly explains the section's giver who has no favor to be repaid.
luna: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, specifying the contrast between sincere giving and a gift used to claim a favor.

luna: This condemns spending followed by reminders and injury, or for show; it reverses the section's gift made solely for purification and God's face. | terra: Charity ruined by reproach, injury, and display reverses the pure gift for God's face, showing that outward giving alone does not establish the good direction.

luna: Those who spend seeking God's approval and to strengthen themselves are compared to a garden on high ground; the motive directly parallels the section's gift for the Lord's face. | terra: Those who spend seeking God's pleasure and inner firmness are likened to a fruitful elevated garden, the positive motive and outcome opposed to 2:264's barren display.

luna: Spending is for one's own good and is done ابتغاء وجه الله; the verse directly connects giving with seeking God's face, as in the section. | terra: This ayah joins the boundary لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَاهُمْ, God's guidance, spending solely for وَجْهِ اللَّهِ, and full repayment, matching the good runner's direction, gift, motive, and finish.

luna: The verse says disbelievers' wealth and children will not avail them against God and names the Fire; this directly echoes the section's question about wealth when a person falls. | terra: Wealth and children will not avail the unbelievers before God, and the ayah names them as fuel of the Fire, joining failed means to destination.

luna: One does not attain righteousness until spending what one loves; this specifies the cost of the section's giving. | terra: The runner cannot attain righteousness until spending from what he loves, making generosity a required crossing toward the good end.
terra: اعْتَصِمُوا ... جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا commands maintained joining and recalls God joining hostile hearts, the positive opposite of the section's opened seam.
terra: The command not to be like those who تَفَرَّقُوا after clear signs identifies blameworthy division as a preventable reversal of communal cohesion.
luna: The same wealth-and-children formula is applied to disbelievers and followed by the Fire, restating the section's limit on wealth at the end of a course.

luna: سَارِعُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ and a Garden gives the section's running a specific righteous destination. | terra: وَسَارِعُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ directs rapid movement toward forgiveness and Garden, another explicit good-course command with destination.
luna: Those who spend in ease and hardship are described as God-fearing, joining the section's generosity with its two conditions and its taqwa.
terra: The respite granted to unbelievers is not good for them but lets sin increase, distinguishing ease of continuation from goodness of destination.

luna: The verse condemns those who withhold God's bounty and calls their assumed good evil; it directly develops the miser's path and its reversal. | terra: Miserly people think withholding is good for them, but it is evil and what they withheld becomes a collar; the ayah exposes felt advantage as the bad course's deception.
luna: It names the stingy, those who urge others to stinginess, and those who conceal God's bounty; this adds concealment and social influence to the section's miserly course.
luna: Spending to be seen by people is named here, a specific opposite to the section's giver who seeks only God's face.
terra: نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ states that God turns the dissenter toward what he chose, then brings him to Hell; it closely matches facilitation in the runner's selected direction.
luna: Believers are told to fear God, seek a means to Him, and strive in His way; the verse brings taqwa, directed effort, and a path into one command.

luna: This verse says communities have distinct law and way, commands فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ, and says all return to God; it brings divergence, directed striving, and its end together. | terra: The ayah joins distinct ways, a command to race in good deeds, common return to God, and disclosure of اختلاف; it gathers the section's directions, race, finish, and revealed difference in one scene.
terra: When warning is forgotten, the gates of everything are opened until the people rejoice and are seized suddenly, making apparent provision the smooth approach to an unseen end.
terra: People come to God فُرَادَىٰ and leave behind what was granted them, joining solitary arrival to the failure of possessions at the finish.

luna: God opens one person's chest to Islam but makes another's constricted as though climbing heaven; this gives an inward experience of ease and difficulty alongside the section's route metaphor. | terra: God opens the breast of the one guided and makes the breast of the one led astray tight كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ, rendering opposed guidance as bodily ease and arduous ascent.
terra: Each has degrees according to deeds, turning the section's disparate efforts into correspondingly graded outcomes.

luna: The command to follow صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا and not follow other paths makes the section's straight course and divergent alternatives a direct choice. | terra: God's straight path is singular, while following السُّبُلَ makes people تَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ from it; the ayah explicitly joins road choice to dispersal.

luna: This condemns those who split their religion into sects; its schismatic division is a contrasting sense of separation beside the section's varied courses. | terra: Those who split their religion into factions stand outside the Messenger's responsibility, another concrete religious form of courses whose cohesion has broken.
luna: Satan says he will sit on God's straight path to obstruct it, making opposition to the guided course explicit.
luna: Satan's approach from before, behind, right, and left recalls the section's dictionary list of direction, front, and back; it shows temptation coming from every side of the path.
terra: One group is guided and the other deserves error after taking devils as allies while thinking themselves guided, a direct two-group version of deceptive directional ease.
terra: Those who obstruct God's way and seek it عِوَجًا turn a straight-directed road into a crooked one, clarifying the image's iltiwā' by explicit opposition.
terra: The arrogant refuse the way of right guidance even when they see it, but adopt the way of error when they see it, explicitly staging recognition followed by contrary route choice.
terra: Twelve tribes and twelve springs again organize each group around its known drinking place, illuminating a Quranic boundary to the section's single-source departure image.
terra: The same divine gradual drawing from where deniers do not know repeats the section's insight that movement toward the hard end can feel unimpeded.
luna: The command not to turn one's back in battle uses the turn-away family in a physical retreat sense, contrasting with the section's denier who turns away from guidance.
luna: The next verse gives punishment for turning one's back except for a tactical maneuver, making the physical retreat and its consequence explicit.
terra: أَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ makes divine joining of hearts the exact relational opposite of hearts that are shattā and groups whose adhesion has lifted.
luna: Those who hoard gold and silver without spending in God's way are warned of painful punishment, a direct opposite to the section's giver and a concrete form of miserliness.
luna: The next verse says the hoarded metal will be heated and used to brand its owners, then calls it what they hoarded; it makes the miser's wealth itself part of the outcome.
terra: Wealth and children that inspire admiration are described as means by which God lets deniers be tormented and die unbelieving, another reversal of apparent worldly ease.
terra: Some covenant that if given bounty they will give charity and be righteous, setting up a promised good direction under provision.

luna: After receiving God's bounty, these people became miserly and turned away; it joins the section's bukhul and tawalla in one account. | terra: When bounty arrives they become miserly and تَوَلَّوا, showing a gift followed by the same withholding and turn that define the wrong branch.
terra: Some spending is taken as a means of nearness to God and the Messenger's prayers, so the gift itself becomes directed travel toward divine mercy.

luna: The early forerunners are followed by people who follow them well, and God is pleased with them; this joins the section's racing image to the satisfaction of its ending. | terra: السَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ combines the racers who pass ahead with the “first” root, then ends with reciprocal divine pleasure, uniting the section's race, order, and satisfaction.

luna: The command to take charity from people's wealth, تَطْهِيرًا وَتُزَكِّيهِم, directly joins wealth-giving to purification. | terra: Charity is taken مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ to purify and تزكيهم, directly unpacking how giving wealth can be the act of self-purification in 92:18.
terra: The command to work is followed by God's seeing the work and eventual disclosure of it, closely paralleling sa'y that will be seen and repaid.
terra: A structure founded on a collapsing bank falls with its builder into Hell, a vivid nonlexical realization of the section's unnoticed downhill course and terminal plunge.
luna: God begins creation and repeats it, with all returning to Him; this gives a creation-to-return arc beside the section's first and last and its race endpoint.
terra: Those content and satisfied with the nearer life reverse the section's final satisfaction: their riḍā attaches to the passing start rather than the lasting finish.
terra: Fire becomes the refuge earned by that misplaced satisfaction, exposing its terminal reversal.
terra: The question whether the one who guides to truth is more worthy to be followed focuses the section's directional image on choosing a guide.
terra: After truth comes from the Lord, whoever accepts guidance does so for himself and whoever strays does so against himself, assigning the consequences of direction to each traveler.
terra: Those who desire the nearer life receive their works there in full, showing a chosen direction provisionally paid along its own course.
terra: The same worldly-directed group has only Fire in the Hereafter and its deeds fail, revealing the course's actual terminal difficulty.
terra: The same obstruction and search for عِوَجًا is tied to denial of the Hereafter, connecting crookedness of course to rejection of its finish.
terra: At the arriving Day, humanity divides into شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ, making final wretchedness and happiness the revealed forms of divergent courses.
terra: Those made wretched are in the Fire, giving one class named in 11:105 its destination.
terra: Those made happy are in the Garden, giving the opposed class its enduring destination.

terra: Joseph's brothers report that they went racing, a literal human contest that illustrates the competitive branch of the section's race vocabulary, though it occurs inside their deceptive account.
terra: Joseph and the woman race to the same door with opposite aims, a precise scene in which shared direction and speed conceal contrary moral courses.
terra: Neighboring plots are watered بِمَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ yet yield preferred and differing fruit, a natural analogue to distinct outcomes emerging around one shared water source.
terra: Those seeking their Lord's face remain patient, pray, and spend secretly and openly; the shared motive makes these acts a fuller portrait of the good runner's direction.
terra: Those who prefer the nearer life and seek God's way عِوَجًا combine temporal preference with making the road crooked, the section's twisted usr-course stated directly.
luna: The speakers say God has guided them سُبُلَنَا, then resolve to endure and trust Him; this links the section's plural paths with guidance and the response of trust.

luna: قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ is set against a deviating way, while guidance is attributed to God; this states the straight-versus-crooked boundary in the section. | terra: وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ directly matches the section's “upon Us is guidance,” while وَمِنْهَا جَائِرٌ sets the straight-directed road against a deviating one.
terra: A powerless dependent is contrasted with one given good provision who spends from it openly and secretly, presenting two unequal human conditions centered on the use of provision.
terra: A burdensome mute is contrasted with one who commands justice and stands on a straight path, continuing the paired-person image with explicit road language.
terra: Whoever is guided is guided for himself and whoever strays bears his own loss, another exact formulation of personally owned direction.

luna: The person who desires the fleeting life is given a limited portion and then faces Hell; 17:19 contrasts the afterlife-directed striving, paralleling the section's two aims and outcomes. | terra: One who aims at the immediate life is sped toward what God allots and then toward Hell, a precise instance of a runner being carried along the chosen bad direction.

luna: This verse names the one who desires the Hereafter and سَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا, then says that effort is appreciated; 17:18 supplies the contrasting worldly aim. | terra: One who aims at the Hereafter and سَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا has that effort thanked, directly joining intention, proper running, and the good finish.
terra: God says كُلًّا نُمِدُّ, extending provision to both groups named in 17:18-19; this clarifies how divine enabling can accompany opposite human directions.

luna: The verse says each acts according to his own شَاكِلَتِهِ and God knows best who is better guided; this gives individual conduct a distinct direction, as in the section's divergent efforts. | terra: كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِ states that each acts from a distinct disposition, while أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًا judges which resulting course is better directed.
luna: The verse says people would still withhold even if they owned the treasuries of their Lord's mercy; it gives a concrete form to the section's self-sufficient miser.
luna: The choice “whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve” is followed by the fire prepared for wrongdoers, explicitly dividing human courses and outcomes.

luna: Wealth and children are the adornment of worldly life, while enduring good deeds are better in reward and hope; this sharpens the section's contrast between wealth and the course that lasts. | terra: Wealth and children are the adornment of the nearer life, while lasting righteous deeds are better in reward and hope, separating passing provision from the enduring finish.
luna: The next account says the record leaves nothing small or great uncounted and that people find their deeds present, making visible the efforts for which they are repaid.
luna: The person reminded of God's signs فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا turns away and forgets what his hands sent ahead, joining the section's turning away to neglected deeds.

luna: For one who believes and acts well, this verse promises the best reward and يسرًا; it links a good course to ease, unlike the section's difficult course. | terra: The believing doer of good is promised that the ruler will speak to him from his command with ease, another personal promise of yusr following chosen action.

luna: The question introduces the greatest losers in deeds; 18:104 identifies their lost effort and mistaken confidence. | terra: The question about the greatest losers in deeds prepares a judgment of effort by destination rather than by the runner's confidence.

luna: سَعْيُهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا names efforts lost in worldly life even while their agents think they act well, a direct contrary path to the section's fruitful striving. | terra: ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ describes effort itself going astray in the nearer life while its runners think they do good, the section's unnoticed acceleration down the wrong way.

luna: The next verse says those losers denied their Lord's signs and meeting Him, explaining the wasted deeds announced in 18:104. | terra: The misdirected effort of 18:104 ends in works made void and given no weight, specifying why confident motion was actually loss.

luna: The promise is described as مَأْتِيًّا, something arriving; this recalls the section's dictionary sense of a finish or endpoint in the ء ت ي family, though the verse speaks of a promised Garden.
luna: The next verse identifies the promised inheritance as the Garden for God's servants who fear Him, supplying the destination after 19:61.
terra: The Merciful extends the one in error further until the promised end is seen, a close parallel to allowing a wrong-directed runner to proceed easily toward disclosure.
terra: وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى gives the opposing increase to those guided, forming with 19:75 two divinely extended directions.
terra: The Godfearing are gathered to the Merciful وَفْدًا, a dignified procession at the end of their directed course.
terra: The criminals are driven to Hell وِرْدًا, a thirsty counter-procession that recalls the section's watering-place departure while reversing its destination.
terra: Each creature comes to God يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَرْدًا; solitary arrival joins the source section's finish-line sense of the ء-ت-y family to the dispersal of former groups.
terra: God makes the Quran easy in the Messenger's tongue to give good news to the Godfearing and warn opponents, joining taysir to communication addressed toward two responses.

luna: The Hour is coming so that every soul may be repaid for what it strives for; this directly joins the section's striving to its final reckoning. | terra: The Hour comes so every soul may be repaid بِمَا تَسْعَىٰ, directly making sa'y the measured substance of final recompense.
terra: Moses is warned not to be turned from the Hour by one following desire فَتَرْدَىٰ; the same r-d-y root makes diversion end in ruin.

luna: Moses asks وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي, using facilitation for a task rather than a road; it clarifies the section's prepared/eased sense. | terra: Moses asks وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي, using the section's taysīr root for making a commissioned task ready and manageable rather than for a whole life-road.
terra: Punishment is placed upon مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ, exactly reproducing the paired denial and turning-away that identify surah 92's bad runner.
terra: Whoever follows God's guidance neither strays nor suffers, a divine statement joining the shown direction to the character of its route.
terra: Whoever turns away from God's reminder receives a constricted life and blind resurrection, giving the opposite orientation its hard end.
luna: They يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ while calling in hope and fear, joining swift effort with the section's God-fearing orientation.
terra: People cut their affair apart while كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَاجِعُونَ, joining division in the course to a single divine point of return.
terra: The believer who does righteous deeds finds لَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِ and the effort written, securing the good runner's work against loss.
terra: A devil appointed as ally will mislead its follower and يَهْدِيهِ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ السَّعِيرِ; “guiding” to Blaze is the dark reversal of guidance to the good end.
terra: One who associates partners with God is pictured as falling from the sky and being snatched or blown far away, a vivid plunge after losing a unified divine direction.
terra: Communities cut their affair into separate books and each party rejoices in its own, an inwardly confident form of the section's scattered directions.
terra: The question asks whether wealth and sons supplied to deniers are being mistaken for a hastening of good.
terra: The answer that they do not perceive corrects the runner's reading of worldly facilitation as proof of a good destination.
terra: Those who يُؤْتُونَ مَا آتَوا give while their hearts fear return to their Lord, joining gift, fear, and the anticipated finish.

luna: These people يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ and are foremost in them, a specific image of directed eagerness toward good. | terra: أُولَٰئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ explicitly turns the fearful givers of 23:60 into racers and forerunners.
terra: The Day is عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ عَسِيرًا, another occurrence where difficulty names the unbelievers' final day rather than a temporary obstacle.
luna: The Messenger says he asks no recompense and points to whoever takes a way to the Lord; this links the section's unrepaid giving with a directed path.
terra: يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ generalizes the section's failed wealth to the Day when neither wealth nor children benefit.
terra: The exception إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ replaces failed wealth with a sound heart as what matters at arrival.
terra: God beautifies the deeds of those without faith in the Hereafter so they wander blindly, a specific mechanism for the wrong course feeling fit to its traveler.
terra: The commanded reciter says that the guided person is guided for himself, while his role toward one who strays is warning, distinguishing divine direction, human choice, and messenger stance.
terra: A man comes مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ to warn Moses, embodying sa'y as swift purposeful travel from a distant point.
luna: The verse stages people watering flocks at a well and two women held apart from the crowd, recalling the section's shared watering place; it does not show the later dispersal.
luna: Moses waters the women's flock at that same well, completing the watering scene linked to 28:23 without depicting people leaving in separate bands.

luna: The verse tells the Messenger that he cannot guide whom he loves, while God guides whom He wills; it specifies divine responsibility in the guidance claim. | terra: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ contrasts the Messenger's limit with God's act of guiding, clarifying who bears the “upon Us” statement in 92:12.
terra: لَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْأُولَىٰ وَالْآخِرَةِ places both first and later under God and adds judgment and return, matching the race's two temporal bounds and judge.
luna: What God has given is to be used to seek the Hereafter while doing good; this makes wealth a means of choosing a lasting destination.
terra: Satan beautifies past peoples' deeds and bars them from السَّبِيل despite their perceptiveness, another explicit case of capable runners diverted without recognizing the course.

luna: Those who strive for God are promised guidance to سُبُلَنَا; the verse joins exertion to God's direction through multiple ways. | terra: Those who strive toward God are answered لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا, directly linking exertion with divine guidance into roads.
terra: لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ states divine ownership across “before” and “after” without the same roots, a nonlexical parallel to ownership of both race-ends.

luna: On the Day of Resurrection people يَتَفَرَّقُونَ, a direct parallel to the section's dispersed people and divided directions. | terra: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ gives the other explicit Resurrection-day separation named by the section, when a formerly common company breaks into final groups.

luna: The next verse puts the believers in a garden rejoicing, completing one side of the split in 30:14. | terra: After the separation of 30:14, believers who did good are delighted in a meadow, so this row supplies one separated group's own destination.

luna: The paired next verse assigns the rejecters to punishment, completing the other side of 30:14. | terra: After the same separation, deniers are brought to punishment, supplying the other group's destination.
terra: Those who split religion become sects, كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ, showing separate companies mistaking their local satisfaction for the true finish.
terra: Giving the due of kin, poor, and traveler is declared best for those seeking God's face, directly joining concrete gifts to the motive in 92:20.
terra: Giving zakat while seeking وَجْهَ اللَّهِ joins gift, pure direction, and increase, closely matching the motive and result of 92:18-20.
luna: The command to face the upright religion is followed by the day when people will be separated; it joins orientation to the section's division into courses.

luna: Neither wealth nor children bring people near to God; belief and righteous action do, with multiplied reward. This directly distinguishes the section's wealth from the effort that reaches its end.
terra: One whose evil work is beautified sees it as good; this is the inward mechanism by which the hard destination can feel like an easy road.

luna: Among those inheriting the Book are a wrongdoer, a moderate one, and a foremost one in good deeds; this gives a specific threefold spread of human efforts. | terra: One inherited Book yields a self-wronger, a moderate person, and one سَابِقٌ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ, a direct picture of disparate efforts emerging from a shared gift.
terra: A man likewise comes مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ to direct his people toward the messengers, joining literal running with urgent guidance.
terra: From the graves إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَنسِلُونَ stages rapid common departure toward the Lord, the final version of runners leaving one point for a goal.
terra: No soul is wronged and each is recompensed only for what it did, explaining the judgment awaiting those who hasten from the graves in 36:51.
terra: God's covenant not to worship Satan identifies an alternative leader on the road and calls him an evident enemy.
terra: وَأَنِ اعْبُدُونِي هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ sets the straight route of worship directly against the satanic course prohibited in 36:60.
terra: If God erased their eyes they would race for the path yet be unable to see; the ayah sharply separates speed toward a road from genuine guidance on it.
terra: The command to gather wrongdoers and their kinds forms the company that the next ayah directs onto the road to Hell.
terra: فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ uses guidance language for conveyance to Hell, a stark reversal that makes destination essential to judging guidance.
luna: The phrase لَتُرْدِينِ uses the ر د ي family for ruining someone; this is a different, destructive sense beside the section's dictionary image of a horse speeding.
terra: لِمِثْلِ هَٰذَا فَلْيَعْمَلِ الْعَامِلُونَ directs work toward the saving outcome just described, a work-centered counterpart to racing for it.

terra: The source-section root sense makes sa'y a race, while بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعْيَ names the son's reaching the capacity for shared labor; it shows sa'y can also join two workers rather than scatter them.
terra: A man belonging to quarrelling partners is contrasted with one wholly devoted to a single master, an inward image of scattered claims versus unified direction.
terra: The Book is sent in truth, after which guidance benefits its receiver and error harms its chooser; the Messenger is not made guardian over them.
terra: The trumpet causes death and then universal rising, beginning the final procession that later divides into companies bound for Hell and Garden.
terra: The earth shines, the record is placed, witnesses are brought, and judgment is rendered before every soul is paid and the companies depart.
terra: Every soul is fully paid for what it did, stating the judgment that separates the two processions of 39:71 and 39:73.
terra: Those who disbelieved are driven to Hell زُمَرًا, a procession in groups along the bad route to its gate.
terra: Those who feared their Lord are driven to the Garden زُمَرًا, the corresponding procession of groups along the opposite route.
terra: Thamud are guided but فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَىٰ عَلَى الْهُدَىٰ, making the wrong route a preference exercised after direction is shown.
luna: The verse says their assumption فَأَرْدَاكُمْ ruined them; this makes the destructive sense of the section's horse-speed root consequential rather than forward motion.
terra: Whoever does right benefits himself and whoever does evil harms himself, a non-road formulation of individually owned moral courses.
terra: The Day of Gathering resolves into فَرِيقٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَفَرِيقٌ فِي السَّعِيرِ, making two final companies out of one assembly.

terra: One who wants the harvest of the Hereafter has it increased, while one who wants the worldly harvest receives some but no share later, a complete pair of intended directions and apportioned ends.
terra: وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ gives the Messenger a real derivative role of directing to God's straight path, complementing rather than erasing divine guidance.
terra: The straight path of 42:52 is God's path and all affairs end with Him, supplying that guided road with its owner and terminus.
terra: Whoever turns blindly from the Reminder is assigned a devil companion, showing a wrong orientation being furnished with its own escort.
terra: The companions bar them from السَّبِيل while they يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ, precisely exposing the bad road that feels right to its runner.
terra: Arrival before God reveals the companion's true distance, so unnoticed misdirection becomes visible only at the finish.
terra: Sharing punishment is the destination disclosed after the wrongly guided pair arrives, completing the course begun in 43:36.
terra: God makes the revelation easy in the Messenger's tongue so people may remember, another defined object prepared for its intended human use.

luna: Good is for oneself and evil against oneself, followed by return to the Lord; this states the consequence of the section's divergent good and bad striving. | terra: Good and evil work return upon their doer before all are returned to the Lord, repeating the personal consequence and common finish of divergent effort.
luna: The command to follow the clear شَرِيعَة and not people's desires presents a prepared way and a choice about which course to follow.
terra: Each has degrees according to what they did and all are fully repaid, a direct statement that differing works become differing ranks without injustice.
terra: Those already guided receive increased guidance and taqwa, showing divine preparation intensifying the direction a runner has taken.

luna: The verse calls people to spend and names the one who is stingy; it says withholding harms only the self, exposing the false self-sufficiency paired with miserliness in the section. | terra: The call to spend exposes miserliness, then warns that if people تَتَوَلَّوْا God will replace them; withholding and turning away converge as in surah 92's bad branch.
terra: The earth splits, people emerge سِرَاعًا, and God calls that gathering عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ; swift motion and divine ease meet at Resurrection.
terra: The ships or bearers that run يُسْرًا unite motion with ease in one compact image, a concrete counterpart to a runner whose course has been made smooth.
luna: The God-fearing are said to reserve a right in their wealth for the asker and deprived, specifying the generosity of the pious course.

luna: لِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَىٰ gives God both terms the section reads as the two ends of a course and as the life here and hereafter. | terra: فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَىٰ is the direct verbal counterpart of 92:13 and places both temporal ends of the race under God's ownership.
luna: تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكْرِنَا names turning away from God's reminder together with wanting worldly life alone, closely matching the section's denier who turns away.
luna: The next verse speaks of straying from God's way and being guided, completing the directional contrast behind the turn in 53:29.
terra: أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ introduces a runner defined by turning away, directly recalling the section's directional reading of tawallā.
terra: وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَىٰ shows giving that stops short, a precise boundary against the sustained giving course of surah 92.

luna: The section treats سَعْي as every good or evil effort; this verse makes a person's share depend on مَا سَعَىٰ. | terra: The section defines every good or evil deed as sa'y; this ayah makes مَا سَعَىٰ the only effort a human can claim, fixing responsibility to each runner's chosen course.

luna: The next verse says سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ; it directly joins the section's effort to its image of deeds becoming visible. | terra: The runner's effort will be seen, وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ, so the divergent courses of 92:4 do not remain hidden at the finish.

luna: The linked verse gives the full recompense after the striving is seen, completing the effort-to-outcome sequence behind the two paths. | terra: This ayah gives the preceding seen effort its full recompense, completing the section's movement from sa'y through judgment to final satisfaction.
terra: The final limit is to the Lord, a concise statement of the divine finish line enclosing every human course.
terra: People emerge from graves كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ, another concrete Resurrection image of a common multitude becoming spread out.
terra: They hurry toward the caller while unbelievers say هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ, joining rapid final motion to the difficult day at its end.
terra: وَكُنتُمْ أَزْوَاجًا ثَلَاثَةً explicitly turns humanity into three final kinds, extending the section's separation image beyond a simple pair.
terra: The companions of the right are the first named company after the threefold division, locating one finish-side.
terra: The companions of the left are the opposed company after the division, locating the contrary finish-side.

luna: وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ names the foremost as racers, matching the section's competitive sense of sa'y. | terra: وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ names the racers who have passed ahead, directly activating the section's secondary competitive sense of sa'y.

luna: The next verse identifies those forerunners as the brought-near, supplying what being first in 56:10 leads to. | terra: أُولَٰئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ supplies the destination of the forerunners named in 56:10: passing ahead ends in nearness.

luna: The verse calls God الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ; this uses the same first/last pair as divine attributes, distinct from the section's temporal or race-end sense. | terra: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ applies the section's beginning/end roots to God Himself, suggesting that every temporal race is enclosed by the First and the Last.
terra: Those who spent and fought before the victory outrank later participants though all receive good, adding precedence and order within the good race without denying later runners.
terra: On the final Day the believers' light يَسْعَىٰ before and beside them toward good news of Gardens, giving sa'y a luminous motion at the good finish.
terra: A wall separates believers whose light runs ahead from hypocrites asking to borrow it, turning divergent final motion into a visible barrier.
luna: Men and women who give charity are promised multiplied reward, a direct giving-to-recompense parallel to the section's course.

luna: The verse calls worldly life play and adornment and contrasts it with the lasting Hereafter, giving the section's first/last division a concrete value. | terra: The nearer life is a brief, competitive display that becomes dry debris; this tells the runners what passes before 57:21 commands the race toward what remains.

luna: The command سَابِقُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ and a Garden makes racing toward a final reward explicit. | terra: سَابِقُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ commands a race toward forgiveness and Garden, supplying the good course with an explicit finish line.
luna: This verse describes the stingy and those who urge stinginess, then says God is self-sufficient; it exposes the false human self-sufficiency paired with withholding in the section.

luna: Wealth and children will not avail people against God, and they are assigned to the Fire; this is another direct formulation of the failure of wealth in the section's reckoning. | terra: Neither wealth nor children avail against God, and those who relied on them become companions of the Fire, another direct boundary on the bad runner's resources.
terra: Those protected from the stinginess of their own souls are the successful, directly linking escape from miserliness to reaching the good end.

luna: شَتَّىٰ describes hearts that are divided despite appearing united; this transfers the section's dispersal from people on a road to inward separation. | terra: تَحْسَبُهُمْ جَمِيعًا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّىٰ makes the section's opened seam inward: visible togetherness can conceal truly scattered hearts.
terra: The companions of Fire and Garden are declared unequal, fixing the boundary that prevents apparently similar earthly motion from flattening the two ends.

luna: فَاسْعَوْا commands people to hasten toward Friday remembrance and leave trade; the same sa'y word now gathers them toward one shared direction. | terra: فَاسْعَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ uses sa'y as commanded purposeful quick movement toward a named goal, grounding the section's physical dictionary sense.

luna: After prayer, people are told to disperse through the land and seek God's bounty; this reverses the gathering of 62:9 and closely recalls people leaving one watering place for separate aims. | terra: After common prayer, فَانتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ sends people dispersing into the land to seek God's bounty, a close enacted analogue to departure from a shared stopping place.

luna: The warning not to let wealth and children distract from God's remembrance fits the section's self-sufficient person whose wealth cannot save him. | terra: Believers are warned not to let wealth and children distract them from God's remembrance, because that apparent abundance can direct them into loss.
luna: People are urged to spend from what God provided before death comes, a precise link to the section's giver and its warning about the moment a person falls.
luna: The next verse says no soul's appointed time is delayed and God knows what people do, completing the urgency of spending before death in 63:10.
terra: Wealth and children are named as a test immediately before the command to fear, spend, and overcome stinginess, identifying the material crossroads.

luna: Spend from what God provided and whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul succeeds; this directly reverses the section's miserly path. | terra: Fear, attentive obedience, and spending are joined to success through protection from one's own stinginess, compactly restating the good course against the miserly one.
terra: A good loan to God is multiplied and forgiven, giving the preceding act of spending its divinely enlarged finish.
terra: سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا makes God bring ease after hardship, reversing the section's spatial two-road picture into a temporal transformation.
terra: The believers' light يَسْعَىٰ before them as they ask God to perfect it, staging directed final motion together with dependence on divine completion.

luna: The contrast between one walking face-down and one walking upright on a straight path makes moral direction visible as bodily movement. | terra: The ayah contrasts one walking fallen on his face with one walking سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ, making bodily gait reveal which course is truly guided.
terra: The garden owners swear to harvest in the morning, beginning a purposeful early journey whose concealed aim will disclose its moral direction.
terra: The garden owners make no saving qualification to their oath, exposing the closed confidence with which they commit to the withholding plan.
terra: Their call to go early to the crop turns intent into coordinated movement toward a material goal.
terra: They set out whispering, so the common outward course carries a hidden shared resolve.
terra: Their resolve that no poor person enter identifies withholding as the direction of their energetic journey.
terra: They go early confident in their power, a close picture of the bad course feeling ready and controllable to its runners.
terra: At sight of the ruined garden they say they have gone astray, so arrival exposes that their apparently sure course missed its goal.
terra: They correct themselves by admitting deprivation, recognizing the true outcome of the withholding course.
terra: Their confession of transgression turns final loss into moral self-recognition rather than a mere navigational mistake.
terra: They turn desire toward their Lord for something better, showing a newly chosen direction after the first course collapses.
terra: The passage names this an earthly punishment and the Hereafter's punishment greater, connecting the failed run to its ultimate end.
terra: God says He will draw deniers on gradually from where they do not know, one of the clearest formulations of an easy-seeming wrong road advancing unnoticed.
terra: مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ is the speaker's final realization of 92:11: wealth does not avail at the fall and finish.
terra: People emerge from graves سِرَاعًا كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ, a Resurrection race toward visible goal-markers that turns the section's metaphor into a final scene.
terra: The jinn divide themselves into submitters and deviators, and the submitters تَحَرَّوْا رَشَدًا, deliberately seeking the right direction.
terra: The deviators become fuel for Hell, supplying the other self-described group with its finish.
terra: The trumpet blast identifies the event that makes the following “difficult day” arrive; its own contribution is the starting signal for the final scene.

luna: This calls the coming Day يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ, a difficult-day counterpart to the section's hard course; 74:10 specifies for whom it is not easy. | terra: The section's usr-path becomes يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ at its eschatological end, so difficulty names both course and arriving day.

luna: غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ makes the difficulty explicit for disbelievers, setting a hard outcome against the section's easy course. | terra: عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ denies ease to the unbelievers on that difficult day, exposing the limit of the bad road's apparent ease while it is being traveled.
luna: Then he turned back and became arrogant, directly recalling the section's وَتَوَلَّىٰ; the nearby speech gives a concrete rejection.
luna: The following verse records his dismissing the warning as transmitted magic, specifying the denial linked to his turn in 74:23.
luna: The next claim calls it human speech, further stating how this speaker denies the message after turning away.
terra: The final destination is to the Lord, naming the common terminus toward which the section's divergent runners move.
terra: The human is informed of what he sent ahead and put later, making the ordering of deeds visible at the finish.
terra: وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the exact two acts of 92:16, confirming that rejection is simultaneously a turn in direction.
terra: After denial and turning away, the man goes swaggering to his people; the bodily gait extends his wrongly oriented motion.

luna: The verse says God guided the human to السَّبِيلَ, then divides the response into grateful and ungrateful, making the section's two directed courses explicit. | terra: إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ presents one shown road followed by the alternatives شَاكِرًا and كَفُورًا, the same guidance-before-division relation as the section.
terra: Chains and Blaze state the destination prepared for the ungrateful branch of 76:3, giving that response its road-end.
terra: The righteous drink from a cup at the good branch's destination, supplying a concrete reward before their deeds are recalled.
terra: The spring made to gush by God's servants extends that destination scene and contrasts with the thirsty procession to Hell in 19:86.

luna: They fulfill vows and fear a day's evil, matching the section's God-fearing course; 76:8–10 show the giving and motive that follow. | terra: The righteous fulfill vows and fear the spreading Day, joining committed action and fear on the thankful route.

luna: They give food to needy people, orphans, and captives; this gives a concrete form to the section's act of giving wealth. | terra: They give food despite loving it to the needy, orphan, and captive, concretizing the giving course that surah 92 sketches.

luna: إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ and rejecting reward or thanks directly match giving for God's face without a favor to repay. | terra: لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ and the refusal of جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا directly match giving solely for the Lord's face without seeking repayment.

luna: The next verse restates their fear of the difficult Day, completing the motive behind the giving in 76:8–9. | terra: Their fear of a grim Day explains the direction behind the gift and ties the earthly act to its difficult or easy finish.
terra: At the trumpet people come أَفْوَاجًا, making Resurrection the moment when humanity arrives in distinct companies.
luna: السَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا depicts racers or forerunners; who the agents are is uncertain, but their motion directly recalls the section's competitive running sense.
terra: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ makes Pharaoh's sa'y a running away after he turns his back, a precise negative form of the section's purposeful race.

luna: The section's opening سَعْي is recalled when the great calamity makes a person remember مَا سَعَىٰ. | terra: On the Day of disclosure, the human remembers مَا سَعَىٰ; the runner's whole course becomes present at its finish.
terra: Hell is made visible to whoever sees immediately before the two branches, placing the bad destination at the race's line of sight.

luna: The فَأَمَّا opening introduces a transgressing type, as the section's paired فَأَمَّا/وَأَمَّا clauses sort divergent efforts; the next verses identify this type's preference and end. | terra: فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ opens the first of the same two grammatical and moral branches developed in the section.

luna: Choosing الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا is the opposite orientation to the giver whose course is toward God's pleasure and the Hereafter; 79:39 names its end. | terra: The transgressor يُؤْثِرُ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا, identifying preference for the first life as the motive of the first branch.

luna: The linked side of the two-way account ends at الْجَحِيمَ, supplying the destination for the person who preferred worldly life. | terra: فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَىٰ gives the worldly-preferring branch its final lodging.

luna: The second وَأَمَّا type fears his Lord's standing and restrains desire, a concrete reversal of the transgressor's preference in 79:37–38 and a close parallel to the God-fearing path. | terra: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ opens the opposite branch and grounds its direction in fear of standing before God.

luna: For the God-fearing side, this verse names Paradise as its resting place, completing the paired destinations. | terra: فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَىٰ gives the fearing and self-restraining branch its opposed lodging.
terra: أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَىٰ opens a branch with the same self-sufficiency that marks the withholding course in surah 92.
terra: The addressee attends to the self-sufficient person, showing how human attention can follow the wrong status-marker even when the two inner directions differ.
terra: وَأَمَّا مَن جَاءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ combines the branching frame with purposeful swift approach, staging the section's physical and moral sa'y together.
terra: The approaching runner is وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ, so fear identifies the inward direction of the outward sa'y just as taqwa distinguishes the good course in surah 92.
terra: The addressee is distracted from the fearful runner, completing the scene's reversal between outward prestige and inward direction.
terra: The graves are overturned before every soul learns its record, supplying the bodily release into the final accounting scene.
terra: Every soul learns what it sent ahead and left behind, joining accountable work to the section's first/later and race-order language.

luna: The command فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ الْمُتَنَافِسُونَ makes the section's secondary sense of striving as a contest explicit; its context is the reward of the righteous. | terra: وَفِي ذَٰلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ الْمُتَنَافِسُونَ commands competition for the righteous reward just described, supplying a clearly named object for the race.

luna: كادحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ... فَمُلَاقِيهِ depicts a person striving toward the Lord and meeting Him, a direct image of effort with an endpoint. | terra: Every human is كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ and will meet Him, an exact nonlexical picture of all effort as motion toward an unavoidable finish.
terra: Receiving the book in the right hand identifies the traveler who then receives the easy reckoning of 84:8.
terra: The right-handed runner receives حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا, making ease an attribute of the good course's reckoning and arrival.
terra: The one easily reckoned returns to his people joyful, providing the good route's homecoming and satisfaction.
terra: Receiving the record behind the back begins the opposing route, using bodily orientation to mark the reversed course.
terra: The bad-route traveler calls for destruction, the realized end of a course that had seemed traversable.
terra: وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا supplies the fire at the end of the opposing route, completing the parallel with surah 92's warning.

luna: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ is the same promise of facilitation as the section's path-making verb, addressed to the Prophet. | terra: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ repeats both the divine promise and the y-s-r wording of 92:7, making the Messenger the addressed runner whose course is prepared.
terra: The command to remind follows the promise of facilitation, showing a human act through which divine road-preparation reaches hearers.
terra: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ shows the fearing hearer taking the reminder, the receptive branch after the promise of facilitation in 87:8.
terra: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى names the opposing wretched branch that avoids the reminder, paralleling surah 92's two persons.
terra: The wretched one enters الْنَّارَ الْكُبْرَىٰ, giving the avoided reminder's course its fiery destination.
terra: لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ makes the endpoint a suspension between death and life, revealing the extremity concealed by the apparently easy wrong course.

luna: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ directly connects success with purification, matching the giver who gives wealth to purify himself. | terra: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ links purification to success, directly matching the giver who gives wealth يَتَزَكَّىٰ in surah 92.

luna: The next verse pairs remembrance of the Lord with prayer, specifying the practice that follows purification in 87:14. | terra: Remembering the Lord's name and praying supplies the purified person's positive practice before the worldly/Hereafter contrast.

luna: The following contrast names preferring worldly life, the alternative to the purified course. | terra: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا identifies preference for the nearer life as the choice that bends effort toward the wrong end.

luna: This verse says the Hereafter is better and more enduring, completing the contrast with worldly preference in 87:16 and the section's first/last horizon. | terra: وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ supplies the evaluative difference between the two temporal ends owned by God in 92:13.
terra: Joyful faces introduce the people who are pleased with their sa'y in 88:9, making satisfaction visible at the finish.

luna: لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ joins the section's first action-word سَعْي to its final satisfaction, in one description of the rewarded faces. | terra: لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ explicitly makes faces pleased with their sa'y, joining the section's first action word to its final promised satisfaction.
terra: A high Garden is the dwelling immediately named for the faces pleased with their effort, giving their satisfaction a place.
terra: إِلَّا مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ gives the same identifying turn and disbelief in reversed order, beside the surah that names satisfaction with sa'y.
terra: God's greatest punishment is the destination attached to turning away and disbelief in 88:23.

luna: رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً describes a soul returning to its Lord pleased and pleasing, paralleling the section's final satisfaction. | terra: ارْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً is a direct homeward finish in reciprocal satisfaction, the destination implied by 92:21.

luna: The next verse says to enter among God's servants, continuing the return of the satisfied soul in 89:28. | terra: Entering among God's servants places the returning, satisfied soul into its final company before entry into the Garden.

luna: The sequence ends with entry into God's Garden, supplying the endpoint after the pleased return in 89:28–29. | terra: وَادْخُلِي جَنَّتِي states the place reached by the soul returning pleased and pleasing in 89:28.

luna: النَّجْدَيْنِ gives the section's two ways a concrete counterpart: a human being is shown two elevated routes. | terra: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ is the Quran's explicit pair of shown high roads, the closest external statement of the section's two-way image.

luna: فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ names the steep pass not taken; 90:10 supplies the two elevations, and this verse makes one morally difficult course concrete. | terra: فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ depicts the good way as a steep ascent that must be broken through, correcting the impression that the truly easy end must feel easiest at the start.

luna: The next verse asks what the steep pass is, introducing the deeds that define the difficult way after the two heights in 90:10. | terra: The question وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ pauses over the uphill road and prepares its deeds as the explanation of what traversing it means.

luna: Freedom of a slave is the first deed in the steep pass described after 90:12, giving the difficult route a concrete act of care. | terra: Freeing a neck is the first concrete act on the steep road, giving the shown high way an ethically costly direction.

luna: Feeding during famine continues the steep-pass deeds and recalls the section's emphasis on giving rather than withholding. | terra: Feeding on a day of hunger continues the road as giving under difficulty, directly paralleling the giver's course in surah 92.

luna: The steep-pass description specifies care for an orphan who is related, continuing the route's acts after 90:14. | terra: The orphan of near kin identifies one recipient of the steep-road gift, making the runner's generosity concrete.

luna: It next names a needy person in hardship, extending the concrete acts along the steep route. | terra: The destitute in dust completes the giving scene and shows why the good road can be arduous before its ease.

luna: Faith and mutual counsel to patience and compassion complete the steep-pass deeds, giving the route a moral and relational character. | terra: Faith, mutual patience, and mercy bind the preceding gifts into a sustained communal course rather than an isolated donation.

luna: Those are called أصحاب الميمنة, the right-hand company; after the path's deeds, the verse names one side of the division. | terra: أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ names the company reached by those acts, turning the route into a final side and group.

luna: The next verse names the rejecters as أصحاب المشأمة, the opposite company, completing the split after the steep-pass route. | terra: Those who reject the signs become أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ, the opposing final company formed by the other direction.

luna: The following verse gives that opposite side an enclosed fire as destination, completing the two outcomes opened by the routes. | terra: عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ closes the bad high road with an enclosing fire, matching surah 92's terminal warning.
terra: The soul is inspired with both its depravity and its fear, placing the two moral directions before the runner internally.

luna: The one who زَكَّاهَا succeeds; this directly echoes the section's purification through giving. | terra: Success belongs to the one who purifies the soul, matching the good runner whose gift is made يَتَزَكَّىٰ.

luna: The next verse says the one who دسَّاهَا fails, setting corruption against the successful self-purification of 91:9. | terra: Failure belongs to the one who buries the soul, completing the opposed direction to purification and success.
terra: وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ الْأُولَىٰ uses the same two end-terms and ranks the later one above the first for the addressed Messenger.
terra: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ joins divine giving to future satisfaction, closely echoing the promised pleasure at the section's finish.

luna: With hardship comes ease, a specific pairing that complicates the section's image of two divergent courses; here relief accompanies hardship. | terra: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا puts ease with hardship rather than assigning them to separate routes, a boundary on reading yusr and usr as permanently isolated domains.

luna: The repeated assurance again places ease with hardship, reinforcing that distinct relation rather than the section's forked-road outcome. | terra: The repeated promise that ease accompanies hardship confirms that felt difficulty within the good route need not identify the bad destination.
terra: Humanity is created in the best form, establishing the height from which the following reversal descends.
terra: The human is then returned to the lowest of the low, a stark vertical image of the downward course's end.
terra: Believing good-doers are excepted and receive an unfailing reward, supplying the opposite outcome to that descent.
terra: إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ again makes denial and turning away one coordinated motion, a direct lexical counterpart to the section's bad course.

luna: The final reward includes رَّضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ, closely echoing the section's closing promise that the giver will be satisfied. | terra: God is pleased with the Garden's people and they with Him, and the ayah grounds that end in fear of the Lord, matching fear-directed effort ending in pleasure.

luna: The lexicon's water-side example is people returning in separate groups; here يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ أَشْتَاتًا stages that dispersal on the Day and says they are shown their deeds. | terra: The section's watering-place departure is stated almost verbatim: people يَصْدُرُ ... أَشْتَاتًا on the Day their deeds are shown, turning scattered motion into the disclosure of divergent effort.
terra: After the people depart in groups to see deeds, even an atom's weight of good is seen, specifying the good effort disclosed to each runner.
terra: The paired atom's weight of evil specifies the opposed effort disclosed in the same separated return.

luna: The oath by galloping, panting steeds recalls the section's horse-speed image, though these horses charge rather than race morally or competitively. | terra: The panting chargers make the section's secondary horse-race imagery bodily and audible, showing effort as urgent forward motion.
terra: The horses strike sparks as they run, contributing the friction and force of a course already at speed.
terra: Their dawn charge gives the running a chosen time and objective rather than leaving it as undirected motion.
terra: The raised dust makes a company's rapid passage visible after it has moved through the ground.

luna: The steeds reach the midst of a gathered company, giving the charge in 100:1 a point of arrival; the relation to a race finish remains only an analogy. | terra: The chargers penetrate the center of a host, supplying an attained point at the end of the charge.
terra: The horse scene turns to the human being's ingratitude toward his Lord, revealing the moral direction beneath the display of speed.
terra: The passage makes human ingratitude directly witnessed, so the inward judgment following the charging horses is not speculative.
terra: Intense love of wealth identifies what directs the ungrateful runner, matching the section's miserly reliance on possessions.
terra: The scattering of what is in the graves moves the horse-charge passage to the final emergence where every course is exposed.
terra: What breasts conceal is brought out, so the inner direction of apparently similar outward movement becomes manifest.
terra: The Lord's complete knowledge on that Day closes the charging, wealth, graves, and exposed-hearts sequence with divine appraisal.
terra: People become كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ, a bodily image of the same final dispersal conveyed by أشتات at the watering place.
terra: The condemned person gathers and repeatedly counts wealth, locating his course in accumulation rather than giving.
terra: He supposes his wealth will make him last, stating the false confidence that possessions can defeat the runner's final fall.
terra: His being cast into the Crusher supplies the fiery reversal of that imagined security in wealth.
terra: مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ closely repeats the section's claim that accumulated wealth cannot rescue its owner from the fiery end.
